dervis-irab:21-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرابَ): They set out for its wall and climbed down from the top of it. The sūr is the high wall. The word المحراب has been explained earlier. And الخصم means the disputant and the contender; it may be applied to two persons, to a plural and to a feminine, so one says "the two of them are a khaṣm", "they are a khaṣm" and "she is a khaṣm", because in origin it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). A parallel has already come up, namely ضيف in the verse «حديث ضيف ابراهيم المكرمين».
(وَلا تُشْطِطْ): "and do not act unjustly". It is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the shīn and kasra on the first ṭāʾ, from ashṭaṭa, yushṭiṭu, ishṭāṭan, when one oversteps the limit. Abū ʿUbayda said: "shaṭaṭtu fī l-ḥukm and ashṭaṭtu fīhi" when you act unjustly; so it is among the verbs in which the forms faʿala and afʿala agree.
(سَواءِ الصِّراطِ): the middle of the road, the right course and its highway.
(أَكْفِلْنِيها): "make me her guarantor"; what is meant is "give her to me in possession". In al-Mukhtār: "kafala ʿanhu bi-l-māl li-gharīmihi, and akfalahu l-māl, I made him responsible for it; and kafalahu iyyāhu, with light fā', so he is kāfil, of the pattern naṣara and dakhala; and kaffalahu iyyāhu takfīlan is the same."
(وَعَزَّنِي): "and he overcame me in the dispute", and brought arguments that I am unable to refute. In al-Mukhtār: "ʿazza ʿalayhi: he overcame him, and its pattern is radda. In the proverb «man ʿazza bazza», that is, whoever overcomes plunders. The noun is al-ʿizza, which is strength and mastery. ʿazzahu fī l-khiṭāb and ʿāzzahu mean he overcame him." Majnūn Laylā said:
قطاة عزها شرك فباتت ... تجاذبه وقد علق الجناح
(A sandgrouse caught by a snare spent the night pulling against it, its wing entangled.)
And before it:
كأن القلب ليلة قيل يغدى ... بليلى العامرية أو يراح
(As if the heart, on the night it was said that Laylā of the ʿĀmir tribe would depart in the morning or the evening...)
He likened his heart, when he heard of her departure, to a dove whose wing the snare has seized, in the abundance of its fluttering.
(الْخُلَطاءِ): the partners who have mingled their property; the singular is khalīṭ.
Now, the lexicons have given several meanings for khalīṭ, among them: the one who mixes with, the partner, the people whose affair is one, the spouse, the neighbour and the companion; and a man's khalīṭ is the one who mixes with him, like jalīs, the one who sits with him.

* I'rab:
(وَهَلْ أَتاكَ نَبَأُ الْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرابَ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to relate the story of Dāwūd. هل is a particle of interrogation whose meaning is wonder and eagerness to hear what follows, as you say to the one you address: "Do you know what happened today?" and then tell him what happened. أتاك نبأ الخصم: a past verb, a fronted direct object (mafʿūl bihi) and a postponed agent (fāʿil). إذ is an adverbial for an omitted muḍāf, that is, "the report of the disputing of the disputants when they climbed". The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "If you say: to what is إذ governed in the accusative? I say: it cannot be other than governed by أتاك, or by النبأ, or by something omitted. It is not permissible that it be governed by أتاك, because the coming of the report to the Messenger of Allah can occur only in his own time, not in the time of Dāwūd; nor by النبأ, because the coming of the report took place in the time of Dāwūd, so its coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not be correct; and if you meant by النبأ the story itself, it would not be a governor. So it remains that it is accusative by an omitted word, its implied form being: 'and has the report of the disputants' going to law reached you, when…'. It is also possible that it is governed by الخصم because of the sense of a verb it contains." The clause تسوروا is what the adverbial is annexed to; تسوروا is a past verb and agent, and المحراب is a direct object.
(إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلى داوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ) إذ is a badal (substitute) for the first إذ, and the clause دخلوا is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. على داود: the two are attached to دخلوا. The فاء is a conjunction; فزع is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; منهم: the two are attached to فزع. (قالُوا لا تَخَفْ خَصْمانِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ) The clause is resumptive, introduced as an answer to a question arising from the report of his fright, as if it were said: "So what did they say when they saw the signs of fright imprinted on his face?" So he said: "They said…". لا is prohibitive; تخف is an imperfect verb jussive (majzūm) by لا, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; خصمان is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "we are two disputants"; the clause بغى is an adjective of خصمان; بعضنا is the agent; على بعض: the two are attached to بغى. (فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَنا بِالْحَقِّ وَلا تُشْطِطْ وَاهْدِنا إِلى سَواءِ الصِّراطِ) The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); احكم is an imperative verb with a latent agent; بيننا is an adverbial attached to احكم; بالحق is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or both are attached to احكم as well. ولا تشطط is conjoined to احكم; واهد is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter, with a latent agent whose implied form is "you"; نا is a direct object; إلى سواء الصراط: the two are attached to اهدنا.
(إِنَّ هذا أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِيَ نَعْجَةٌ واحِدَةٌ) إن and its noun; أخي is a badal from هذا, or the khabar of إن; له is a fronted khabar; تسع is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of إن or a second khabar; تسعون is conjoined to تسع; نعجة is a tamyīz (specification); لي is a fronted khabar; نعجة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; واحدة is an adjective. The matter of the metaphorical use of "ewe" will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَقالَ أَكْفِلْنِيها وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطابِ) The فاء is a conjunction; قال is a past verb; the clause أكفلنيها, made up of the verb, the latent agent and the two objects, is the quoted speech; وعزني is conjoined to فقال; في الخطاب: the two are attached to عزني. (قالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلى نِعاجِهِ) The lām introduces the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; ظلمك is a verb with a latent agent, and the كاف is a direct object; بسؤال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظلمك; نعجتك is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive), as an annexation of the maṣdar to its object, the agent being omitted, that is, "by his asking you for your ewe"; إلى نعاجه: the two are attached to an omitted word whose implied form is "to add it". (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْخُلَطاءِ لَيَبْغِي بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and it may also be a ḥāl wāw; إن and its noun; من الخلطاء is an adjective of كثيرا; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); يبغي بعضهم: an imperfect verb and agent; على بعض: the two are attached to يبغي. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ ما هُمْ) إلا is a particle of exception; الذين is a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); عملوا is conjoined to آمنوا; الصالحات is a direct object; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; قليل is a fronted khabar; ما is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasizing the fewness; هم is a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(وَظَنَّ داوُدُ أَنَّما فَتَنَّاهُ فَاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ راكِعاً وَأَنابَ) Conjoined to an omitted clause, that is, "the two angels said: the man has given judgement against himself, so he realized". وظن داود: a verb and agent; إنما: the particle kāffa (restraining) and the restrained one (makfūfa), and it together with what follows it takes the place of the two objects of ظن; وفتناه: a past verb, agent and direct object; فاستغفر is conjoined to وظن; ربه is a direct object; وخر is also conjoined, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; راكعا is a ḥāl; وأناب is also conjoined. (فَغَفَرْنا لَهُ ذلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ) Also conjoined; غفرنا is a verb and agent; له: the two are attached to غفرنا; ذلك is a direct object, that is, that sin. And إن: the wāw is a conjunction, and أن is a particle resembling the verb; له is a fronted khabar; عندنا is an adverbial attached to an omitted word, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the lām is the shifted lām; زلفى is the noun of إن; وحسن مآب is conjoined to زلفى.

* Rhetoric:
In the words «إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة ولي نعجة واحدة» the verse contains a kināya (allusion) for the woman, for they used to allude to a woman by the ewe and the sheep, as in the saying of ʿAntara:
يا شاة ما قنص لمن حلت له ... حرمت علي وليتها لم تحرم
(O sheep, what a prey for the one to whom you are lawful! You were made forbidden to me, and would that you had not been forbidden.)
He only meant the wife of his father, whom he loved; and it is said that she was his slave girl, so he made her unlawful for himself. This kināya agrees with the view that the story proceeds as a parable (tamthīl), and we shall give its summary together with the fabricated fanciful story, in order to free minds from the legends that conflict with the purity and integrity of the prophets.
The story as the commentators relate it:
The people of Dāwūd's time used to ask one another to give up a wife if she pleased him, and he would marry her. The like of this has been reported of the Anṣār, who used to console the Muhājirūn in this way. Dāwūd's eye fell on the wife of Ūriyā and she pleased him, so he asked him to prefer him with her in order to marry her; he was too ashamed before him and gave her up, so he married her and she bore him Sulaymān. It was said to him: "With the multitude of your wives, it was not for you to ask a man who has only one wife to give her up, and it would have been better to overcome desire." And it is said: Ūriyā proposed to her, then Dāwūd proposed, and her family inclined to him, so he came under the one who proposes against the proposal of his brother.
As for what is mentioned, that Dāwūd wished for the rank of his forefathers, and it was said to him that they had been tried and had been patient, so he asked to be tried that he might be patient; and it was said to him: "You will be tried on such and such a day," so he was on his guard that day and shut his sanctuary (miḥrāb) upon himself, whereupon Satan appeared to him in the form of a golden dove, and he stretched out his hand to take it for a young son of his; it flew away and he followed it, and saw a beautiful woman who had let down her hair. So he wrote to Ayyūb ibn Ḥūriyā, the commander of the army of al-Balqāʾ, to send Ūriyā and put him forward before the ark. The one placed forward was forbidden to return until Allah granted victory at his hands or he was martyred. He went forward and greeted, and was ordered to be put forward a second time and a third, and he was killed, and Dāwūd did not grieve over him as one grieves over martyrs, and he married his wife mentioned above. This account is of a kind that it is repugnant to tell even of an ordinary Muslim marked by righteousness, let alone of one of the eminent prophets.
From Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "Whoever tells you the story of Dāwūd as the storytellers relate it, I shall flog him a hundred and sixty lashes, the double of the prescribed punishment for slander."
It is related that a man told this to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz in the presence of a verifying scholar, who called the report false and said: "If the story is as it is in the Book of Allah, then seeking anything contrary to it is slander; and if it is as you have mentioned, and Allah withheld it as a covering for His Prophet, then it is not fitting for you to disclose what Allah has covered." ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: "Hearing these words is dearer to me than everything the sun has risen upon."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What the parable that Allah struck indicates is that his story was nothing but his asking the husband of the woman to give her up to him, and no more." Then al-Zamakhsharī drew attention to the fact that the rebuke came by way of parable and allusion, not explicit statement, and that is because allusion calls for reflection and draws attention to the aspect of the error, while avoiding open rebuke and reprimand. He cast it in the form of a parable so that the person would find it ugly in another and thus make it the measure for finding it ugly in himself, while keeping his dignity, as is advised in a father's way of training his son when some objectionable fault comes from him. He said: And it came in the form of a litigation so that he might rule by his own words «لقد ظلمك», and the proof would be established against him conclusively.
And he said: His words «وهل أتاك» came in the form of a question, to draw attention to the fact that this story is a wondrous one, which deserves to spread and not to be hidden from anyone, and also to arouse eagerness to hear it.
And he said about «في الخطاب»: it may be from mukhāṭaba (addressing), and its meaning is "he came to me with a dispute I could not refute"; and it may be from khiṭba (proposal of marriage) on the pattern mufāʿala, that is, "I proposed and he proposed against my proposal and overcame me", the mufāʿala form being because the proposal issued from both of them.
And he said, on the mention of the ewes, that it is a parable, so their going to law was a parable and their speech was also a parable, because it is more eloquent for the reason given earlier, and to draw attention to the fact that this is a matter one is ashamed to state plainly and that is alluded to because of the ugliness of declaring it, and for the sake of covering Dāwūd, peace be upon him. The aspect of the parable in it is that the story of Ūriyā was likened to a man who has one ewe while his partner has ninety-nine, and he wanted to complete a hundred with that ewe. If you say: the way of the parable is used only when khiṭāb is taken as from khiṭāba (speaking); but if it is from khiṭba, what is its aspect? He said: the aspect then is that the ewe is made a metaphor (istiʿāra) for the woman, as they used the sheep as a metaphor for her in the verse: يا شاة ما قنص لمن حلت له ... (the verse). He said: The difference between parable and metaphor is that on the parable, what first came to Dāwūd's understanding, peace be upon him, was that the litigation was as it appeared, a dispute over ewes, which are cattle, and then through the warning he moved to understand that it was a parable of his own condition; whereas on the metaphor, what he understood from the two men was that the litigation concerned women, expressed by ewes as an allusion, and then he sensed that he was the one meant by it.
I say: Some have reported that this story was not from angels and is not a parable, but was from human beings, either two partners in sheep in reality, or one of them was wealthy with many women, free wives and concubines, while the second was poor with only one wife, and he asked him to give her up. Dāwūd was alarmed, fearing that they might be assassins, since they had come in to him outside the time of judging. Dāwūd's sin was only that he believed one of the two against the other and ascribed wrongdoing to him before asking him.
I say: What this speaker meant by his words was only to clear Dāwūd of a sin to which desire for women would have driven him; so he took the verse in its apparent sense and turned the sin into haste in ascribing wrongdoing to the defendant, because what usually drives to that is the flaring of anger, and its offensiveness is lighter than when what drives to it is lust and passion. Perhaps this speaker supports his view of the verse with the words of Allah the Exalted which follow it as an admonition to Dāwūd, peace be upon him: «يا داود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى». Attention is not given to admonishing him concerning judgements unless what first came from him and became apparent in him was of the kind that had occurred in his judging between people.
The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: "The apparent sense is to keep the word 'ewe' in its real sense, the female of the sheep, and not to use it as an allusion for the woman; there is no necessity calling for that, because that report issued from the angels by way of depicting the case. They gave the example of the story of a man who has one ewe while his partner has ninety-nine, and his companion wanted to complete the water «[Translator's note: the source reads "تتمة الماء", "completing the water"; the context suggests "المائة", the hundred]», so he coveted the ewe of his partner and wanted to take it from him and argued with him over it as one eager to reach his aim argues. This is indicated by his words «وإن كثيرا من الخلطاء». This depiction and parable is more eloquent for the purpose and a clearer indication of what is meant." Until he says: "And what the storytellers related, which contains a belittling of the station of prophethood, we have thrown out, and we are as the poet said:
ونؤثر حكم العقل في كل شبهة ... إذا آثر الاخبار جلاس قصاص
(We prefer the judgement of reason in every doubtful matter, when the companions of storytellers prefer reports.)"

dervis-irab:61-66.t:
* I'rab:
(قالُوا: رَبَّنا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنا هذا فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً فِي النَّارِ) (قالوا) is a verb and agent. (ربنا) is a vocative, a muḍāf (genitive construct) from which the vocative particle has been omitted. (من) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (قدّم) is the khabar (predicate). The (فاء) is a linking particle, because of the scent of the conditional in the relative noun, and the clause (فزده) is the khabar. It is better for (من) to be the object of an omitted verb which what follows explains, that is, "so increase the one who put forward"; or (الهاء) is the first direct object and (عذابا) the second direct object, and (ضعفا) an adjective of (عذابا), meaning "doubled". (في النار) is an adverbial attached to (زده), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the (هاء), that is, "increase it, it being in the Fire", or a second adjective of (عذابا).
(وَقالُوا ما لَنا لا نَرى رِجالًا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِنَ الْأَشْرارِ) (قالوا) is a verb and agent; the pronoun refers to the disbelievers of Mecca such as Abū Jahl, Umayya ibn Khalaf and others. (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; (لنا) is attached to an omitted khabar. The clause (لا نرى) is a ḥāl clause, and the agent of (نرى) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". (رجالا) is a direct object; by them they meant the poor among the Muslims. (كان) and its subject; the clause (كنّا) is an adjective of (رجالا), and the clause (نعدهم) is the khabar of (كنّا), that is, "we reckon them" in this world. (من الأشرار) is attached to (نعدهم).
(أَتَّخَذْناهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصارُ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, and the hamzat al-waṣl dropped because it is not needed. (اتخذناهم) is a past verb, agent, and first direct object, and (سخريا) is the second direct object. It is as though they rebuked themselves for what they used to do in this world. (سخريا) is read with kasra or with ḍamma on the sīn, and the yāʾ is the yāʾ of nisba (relation); thus (السخري) is stronger than (السخر), as was said of (الخصوص) and (خصوصية), to indicate the strength of that. Understand this, for it is good. (أم) is a conjunction connected to His words (مالنا). (زاغت عنهم الأبصار) is a verb and agent, and (عنهم) is attached to (زاغت), so that we did not see them; among them were ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and Salmān. The clause (اتخذناهم) is resumptive.
We see it as useful to quote the words of al-Zamakhsharī. He said: «His words (أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار) have two ways of connection. One is that it connects to His words (ما لنا), that is, "why do we not see them in the Fire?", as though they were not in it, but rather our eyes have swerved from them so that we do not see them while they are in it. They divided their affair between their being among the people of Paradise and their being among the people of the Fire, only that their place was hidden from them. The second way is that it connects to (اتخذناهم سخريا). Either (أم) is the connected one, on the sense of "which of the two acts did we do to them: making them objects of mockery, or despising and belittling them, and that our eyes used to pass over them and look down on them", in the sense of rebuking themselves for both things together. From al-Ḥasan: they did all of that; they took them as objects of mockery, and their eyes swerved from them in contempt of them. Or else (أم) is the disconnected one, as when you say: "It is the camels—or rather, a sheep?" and "Is Zayd with you, or ʿAmr?"»
(إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ) (إن) and its subject, that is, what we have related of them; then the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (حق) is its khabar. (تخاصم أهل النار) is a badal (substitute) for (حق), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause of the omitted mubtadaʾ and its khabar explains the demonstrative noun. The meaning of "disputation" will come in the section on rhetoric.
(قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ) (إنما) is a restricting particle with what it restricts (kāffa and makfūfa); (أنا) is mubtadaʾ and (منذر) the khabar. The (واو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (إله) is genitive in form and nominative in position by virtue of being the mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (الله) is the khabar; and (الواحد القهار) are two adjectives of (الله).
(رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ) (رب) is an adjective or a badal; (وما بينهما) is conjoined to (السموات والأرض); and (العزيز الغفار) are also two adjectives.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار» there is a simile: the exchange of words among them, the dialogue that goes on between them and the questions and answers they trade, is likened to what goes on between disputants, because the leaders' words to their followers «لا مرحبا بهم» and the followers' words «بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم» amount to nothing but the quarrel that disputants hurl at each other.
2- The benefit of a redundant particle in the speech of the Arabs is either in meaning or in wording. The benefit in meaning is to confirm and strengthen the established meaning. The benefit in wording is to adorn the expression and make it more eloquent through its addition, or to make the word or the sentence metrically sound, or give it a fine rhyming prose, or the like. A redundant element may not lack both the verbal and the semantic benefit, otherwise it would be counted as futile. The two benefits may be combined in one particle, and one may occur without the other.

* Benefits:
Changes caused by nisba (relational adjective formation):
We mentioned in the I'rab that (السخري) is stronger than (السخر) and (الخصوصية) stronger than (الخصوص). We mention here that nisba brings about changes in the noun:
1- The addition of the yāʾ of nisba at its end. This doubled yāʾ is a letter in the position of the tāʾ of the feminine, and has no grammatical position.
2- The kasra on the letter before it.
3- Making the yāʾ the end of the noun.
The change in the wording occurs only because of a change in meaning. Do you not see that when you form a nisba from a proper name, it becomes indefinite, so that the definite article can enter it, like the dual and the plural, and it becomes an adjective in the position of a derived word after having been a fixed noun, and the noun after it is made nominative as agent, whether overt or pronominal? You say: "I passed by a Tamīmī man whose father..." and "another, a Hāshimī, whose grandfather...". And when you form a nisba from a maṣdar you add strength to it, as in your saying (سخريا).

dervis-irab:26-29.t:
* I'rab:
(يا داوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to relate what Dāwūd was addressed with after what preceded. You may also posit an omitted saying, conjoined to the words «غفرنا», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «غفرنا», that is, "and We said" or "saying". يا is a vocative particle; داود is the one addressed, a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; إن and its noun; the clause جعلناك is its khabar; جعلناك is a past verb, agent and first direct object; خليفة is the second object of جعلنا; في الأرض is an adjective of خليفة. (فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ) The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); احكم is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; بين الناس: the two are attached to «فاحكم»; بالحق is a ḥāl. (وَلا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَوى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb jussive (majzūm) by لا, with a latent agent whose implied form is "you"; الهوى is a direct object; the فاء is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), since it occurs in the answer to a prohibition; يضلك is an imperfect verb accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to الهوى; the كاف is a direct object; عن سبيل الله: the two are attached to يضلك. Nothing prevents making the فاء a conjunction, with يضلك conjoined to تتبع.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِما نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسابِ) The clause gives the reason for the prohibition against following desire. إن and its noun; the clause يضلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; عن سبيل الله: the two are attached to يضلون; لهم is a fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إن; شديد is an adjective of عذاب; the باء is a preposition, and ما is maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming), interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar governed in the genitive by the باء, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "because of their forgetting"; يوم الحساب is a direct object of نسوا, or an adverbial of the words «لهم عذاب شديد», or a second adjective of it, that is, "they have a severe punishment occurring on the Day of Resurrection because of their forgetting".
(وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما باطِلًا) A resumptive discourse, introduced to confirm the content of what preceded concerning the matter of resurrection, reckoning and recompense. ما is negative; خلقنا is a verb and agent; السماء is a direct object; الأرض is conjoined to السماء; وما بينهما is also conjoined, and the adverbial is attached to an omitted word, the ṣila of ما; باطلا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a vain creation"; it may also be a ḥāl from the agent of خلقنا, that is, "acting in vain" or "possessing vanity".
(ذلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النَّارِ) ذلك, the demonstrative, is a mubtadaʾ, that is, "His creating them in vain", and ظن is its khabar; الذين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive) and the clause كفروا is the ṣila. فويل: the فاء is a conjunction, for ordering the establishment of woe for them upon their vain supposition; ويل is a mubtadaʾ and للذين كفروا is its khabar, and the clause كفروا is the ṣila; من النار is an adjective of ويل. In putting the relative noun in the place of the pronoun «هم» there is an intimation that they deserved the Fire by their disbelief. (أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ كَالْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ) أم is a disjoined conjunction (munqaṭiʿa) and contains the sense of a rhetorical question of denial; نجعل is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; الذين آمنوا is the first object of نجعل, and آمنوا is the ṣila; وعملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا; the كاف is a noun meaning "like", in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of نجعل; في الأرض: the two are attached to المفسدين. (أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الْمُتَّقِينَ كَالْفُجَّارِ) Conjoined to what preceded. In the denial there is a refutation of what they claim, that recompense does not come; for if their words were sound, the state of him who did good and him who did evil, and of him who was godfearing and him who was wicked, would be equal with Allah.
(كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آياتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ) كتاب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "this is a book"; the clause أنزلناه is an adjective; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلناه; مبارك is a second adjective. Some prevented that, on the argument that the non-explicit adjective (the clause) does not precede the explicit adjective, so according to them it is a second khabar or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It was also read مباركا in the accusative, as a permanent ḥāl. ليدبروا: the lām is the lām of reason; يدبروا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason, and the wāw is the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزلناه; آياته is a direct object, that is, "that they may reflect upon them"; وليذكر is conjoined to ليدبروا; أولوا الألباب is the agent.

dervis-irab:67-78.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ) (قل) is a verb, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you, O Muḥammad". The repetition of "say" is to confirm and magnify the tidings. (هو) is mubtadaʾ, (نبأ) khabar, and (عظيم) an adjective.
(أَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ) The clause is a second adjective of (النبأ); it may also be taken as resumptive, to draw attention to the gravity of the offence they commit by turning away from that tiding, namely the Qur'an and the laws and teachings it contains. (أنتم) is mubtadaʾ; (عنه) is attached to (معرضون); and (معرضون) is the khabar of (أنتم).
(ما كانَ لِي مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِالْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ) A resumptive statement, intended to confirm that it is a great tiding coming from Allah the Exalted. (ما) is negative; (كان) is a past incomplete verb; (لي) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (من) is a redundant preposition; (علم) is genitive by (من) in form, in the position of the nominative as the deferred subject of (كان). (بالملا) is attached to (علم), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, that is, "of the tidings of the assembly and their disputing". (الأعلى) is an adjective of (الملا). (إذ) is an adverb of past time, also attached to the maṣdar; al-Zamakhsharī said: «to an omitted word, because the meaning is "I had no knowledge of the speech of the Highest Assembly at the time of their disputing"». The clause (يختصمون) is in the position of the genitive, by the adverb's being annexed to it. It was also said that the pronoun in (يختصمون) refers to Quraysh, that is, they dispute about the matter of the Highest Assembly, because that is a matter beyond the reach of minds to know, and the basis for comprehending it is revelation.
(إِنْ يُوحى إِلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) (إن) is negative; (يوحى) is an imperfect passive verb; (إلي) is attached to (يوحى); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أنما) is a restricting particle with what it restricts, and it, together with what follows it, stands in the place of the deputy agent of (يوحى), that is, "nothing is revealed to me except the warning". The restriction is relative (qaṣr iḍāfī), and it has been repeated here; the discussion of restriction has gone before. (أنا) is mubtadaʾ, (نذير) khabar, and (مبين) an adjective.
(إِذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إِنِّي خالِقٌ بَشَراً مِنْ طِينٍ) (إذ) is a badal (substitute) for the (إذ) of (يختصمون); you may also make it accusative by an omitted "remember". The clause (قال ربك) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. (إن) and what follows is the content of the saying. (إن) and its subject; (خالق) is its khabar; (بشرا) is the direct object of (خالق); and (من طين) is an adjective of (بشرا). This description dispenses with all the human attributes, and that is the mastery of concision.
(فَإِذا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ ساجِدِينَ) The (فاء) is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition. (سويته) is a past verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. (نفخت) is conjoined to (سويته); (فيه) is attached to (نفخت), and likewise His words (من روحي). The meaning is "and I gave him life and made him sentient". (فقعوا): the (فاء) is the linking particle for the apodosis of (إذا); (قعوا) is an imperative verb and agent; (له) is attached to (ساجدين); and (ساجدين) is a ḥāl. By prostration is meant honouring and showing respect.
(فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ) The (فاء) is a conjunction; (سجد الملائكة) is a verb and agent; (كلهم) is the first emphasis (tawkīd) and (أجمعون) the second. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «(كل) is for comprehension and (أجمعون) for togetherness, so both together convey that they prostrated to the last of them, no angel remaining that did not prostrate, and that they prostrated at one time, not separately at different times.»
(إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ اسْتَكْبَرَ وَكانَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ) (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (إبليس) is the excepted, either continuous (muttaṣil) or discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī took a strange view; he said: «If you say: how is Iblīs excepted from the angels when he is of the jinn? I say: he was commanded to prostrate along with them, so they were given preponderance over him in His words (فسجد الملائكة); then he was excepted as one of them is excepted, with a continuous exception.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source, and it is unclear where al-Zamakhsharī's words end; the translation closes the quotation after this sentence.] The clause (استكبر) is resumptive, to explain how he refused to prostrate. (كان) is conjoined to (استكبر); the subject of (كان) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Iblīs; and (من الكافرين) is the khabar of (كان).
(قالَ يا إِبْلِيسُ ما مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ) (قال) is a past verb, its agent referring to Allah the Exalted; (يا) is a vocative particle; (إبليس) is the one addressed, a singular proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma. (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause (منعك) is the khabar. (أن) and what is within its scope are accusative as the second object of (منع); (أن) is a maṣdar particle that causes the accusative; (تسجد) is an imperfect verb made accusative by (أن), its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". The (لام) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, genitive by the (لام); the clause (خلقت) is the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "I created". (بيدي) is attached to (خلقت).
(أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعالِينَ) The hamza is for rebuking, reproachful interrogation, and the hamzat al-waṣl dropped because it is not needed. (استكبرت) is a verb and agent; (أم) is a connected conjunction, and the difference between the two verbs does not prevent that. Sībawayh said: «You say: "Did you strike Zayd or kill him?" Beginning with the verb here is better, because you are asking only about one of the two, not knowing which of them happened, and you are not asking about the place of either, as though you had said: "Which of these happened?"» (كنت): (كان) and its subject; (من العالين) is its khabar, that is, "of the haughty".
(قالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ) (أنا) is mubtadaʾ and (خير) khabar; (منه) is attached to (خير); and the sentence is the content of the saying. (خلقتني) is a verb, agent and direct object; (من نار) is attached to (خلقتني); and (خلقته من طين) is conjoined to (خلقتني من نار).
(قالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْها فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ) (قال) is a past verb whose agent refers to Allah the Exalted. (فاخرج): the (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); (اخرج) is an imperative verb and its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; (منها) is attached to (اخرج). (فإنك): the (فاء) gives the reason for the command to be driven out; (إن) and its subject; (رجيم) is its khabar.
(وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِي إِلى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ) Conjoined to «فإنك رجيم». (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (عليك) is its fronted khabar; (لعنتي) is its deferred subject; and (إلى يوم الدين) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "continuing". The meaning of the termination is that it continues in this world, until when the Day of Judgement comes it is doubled upon him so that the first is almost forgotten, as though it had ended in order to begin anew.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي» the two hands are given preponderance over the other limbs with which works are carried out, because the one who has two hands carries out most of his works with his hands, so that even of an act of the heart it is said, "it is of what your hands have done", figuratively; and so it is said in the proverb «يداك أوكتا وفوك نفخ» ("Your hands tied it and your mouth blew into it"). A group of the Sunnis, such as Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī, refused to regard it as figurative, arguing that the favours of Allah cannot be counted, so how can they be limited by the dual? And that is true. Yet Imām al-Ḥaramayn and others of the Sunnis allowed it to be taken figuratively and answered what Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan mentioned by saying that what is meant is the favour of this world and of the Hereafter; this confirms his preference over Iblīs, since Iblīs was not created for the favour of the Hereafter. And if what is meant is power, then the dual is for magnification, and the like is frequent in the language.

dervis-irab:79-88.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ، قالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ) (قال) is a past verb, its agent a latent pronoun referring to Iblīs. (فأنظرني): the (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), because it discloses an implied condition, whose implied form is "since you have made me accursed, then grant me respite". (أنظرني) is an imperative verb and its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the direct object; (إلى يوم) is attached to (أنظرني); and the clause (يبعثون) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. He asked for a delay in order to lead the children of Ādam astray.
(قالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The (فاء) is a conjunction ordering the content of the sentence upon the granting of respite; the (باء) is a preposition and of oath; (عزتك) is genitive by the (باء), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of oath. The (لام) occurs in the answer to the oath, and (لأغوينهم) is a clause with no grammatical position. (لأغوينهم) is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I", with a direct object, and (أجمعين) is emphasis. [Translator's note: the source writes «وأغويناهم» (with a wāw) in both places for the Qur'anic «لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ»; it is translated here as the Qur'anic word.] (إِلَّا عِبادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ) (إلا) is a particle of exception; (عبادك) is the excepted; (منهم) is a ḥāl; and (المخلصين) is an adjective of (عبادك).
(قالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ) The (فاء) is resumptive; (الحق) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "my oath" or "from me"; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is the truth". And (الحق) is a fronted object of (أقول), that is, "I say only the truth", meaning that the fronting of the object conveyed restriction; or it is a maṣdar confirming the content of His words (لأملأن). The clause (والحق أقول) is parenthetical between the oath and its answer. The first (الحق) has also been read in the accusative.
(لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكَ وَمِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The (لام) is the answer to the oath; (لأملأن) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; and the clause is the khabar of (الحق), or has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. It is not purely the answer to an oath, because it is not explicit in swearing, unlike «لعمرك»; and for this reason the khabar is not obligatorily omitted. (جهنم) is a direct object; (منك) is attached to (لأملأن); (وممن تبعك) is conjoined to (منك); the clause (تبعك) is the ṣila of (من); (منهم) is a ḥāl; and (أجمعين) is emphasis of the pronoun in (منهم), or of the (كاف) in (منك) and what is conjoined to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
«If you ask: what does (أجمعين) emphasise? I say: it must emphasise either the pronoun in (منهم), or the (كاف) in (منك) together with (من تبعك); and the meaning is "I shall fill Hell with the followed and the followers, all of them; I shall leave none of them."»
(قُلْ ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ) (ما) is negative; (أسألكم) is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I", and the (كاف) is the direct object; (عليه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (أجر) and was fronted before it; (من) is a redundant preposition; (أجر) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of (أسألكم). The (واو) is a conjunction or a ḥāl particle; (ما) is a negative of the Ḥijāzī type; (أنا) is its subject; and (من المتكلفين) is its khabar, that is, the pretenders, who claim attributes they do not possess, such that I would feign prophethood and invent the Qur'an. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ) (إن) is negative; (هو) is mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (ذكر) is the khabar of (هو); and (للعالمين) is an adjective of (ذكر). (وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ) The (واو) is a conjunction; the (لام) is the one that prepares for the oath; (تعلمن) is an imperfect verb, nominative because the nūn of emphasis does not directly attach to it, its sign of nominative being the nūn that is omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the omitted (واو), omitted likewise because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. (نبأه) is a direct object; (بعد حين) is an adverb attached to (تعلمن). The verb (علم) here means "to know" (عرف), so it takes one object, which is (نبأه); it may also be taken in its usual sense, in which case the second object is (بعد حين).

dervis-irab:30-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّافِناتُ): the plural of ṣāfina, the horse standing on three legs while resting the other on the edge of the hoof, whether a hind leg or a foreleg. In al-Mukhtār: "The ṣāfin among horses is the one standing on three legs, having set the fourth on the edge of the hoof. The horse ṣafana, of the pattern jalasa. The ṣāfin among people is the one who sets his feet in a row, and its plural is ṣufūn." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "Standing on three legs is hardly found in the crossbreds; it is found only in the pure Arabians. It is also said that He described them with standing and with excellence in order to combine the two praiseworthy qualities, standing and running; that is, when they stand they are calm and at ease in their places, and when they run they are swift and light in their running."
(الْجِيادُ): the plural of jawād, the one that outstrips; and it is said to be the plural of jayyid. In Adab al-Kātib by Ibn Qutayba: "A horse is called ʿatīq, jawād and karīm; and a pack horse, a mule and a donkey are called fāra. The leaders among horses: the first is the sābiq, then the muṣallī, because its head is at the loins (ṣalā) of the sābiq; then the third and the fourth likewise, up to the ninth, and the tenth is the sukayt (also said sukkayt with doubled kāf). What comes after that is not counted, and the fuskul is the one that comes last of the horses in the racecourse." This is what Ibn Qutayba mentioned; they named the third al-mutlī because it follows (yatlū) the second, they named the fourth al-tālī, the fifth al-murtāḥ, the sixth al-ʿāṭif, the seventh al-muʾammal, the eighth al-ḥaẓī and the ninth al-laṭīm.
(مَسْحاً): al-masḥ is cutting. In al-Mukhtār: "masaḥahu bi-l-sayf: he cut him with the sword." (بِالسُّوقِ): the plural of sāq (shin, leg). Among the curious things about the word sāq is that it has many meanings. The first, which is meant here, is the part between the ankle and the knee; it is feminine and its plurals are sūq, sīqān and asūq. The sāq of a tree is its trunk. Among its meanings: sāq al-ḥamām and sāq al-ghurāb are two plants, and sāq ḥurr is the male turtle dove. It is said "the matter was uncovered from its leg", meaning it became severe and grave; "the war stood on a leg", meaning it became fierce; and "the woman bore three sons on one leg", meaning one after another with no girl between them. The discussion on this root is long, so we refer the reader to the lexicons.
(رُخاءً): gentle, good, not violent.
(أَصابَ): he wanted and aimed. In al-Kashshāf: "Al-Aṣmaʿī related from the Arabs: 'aṣāba l-ṣawāb, fa-akhṭaʾa l-jawāb' (he aimed at what was right and missed the answer). And from Ruʾba: two men of the people of the language set out to him to ask him about this word, and he went out to them and said: 'Where are you aiming (tuṣībān)?' They said: 'This is what we were seeking,' and went back. It is also said 'aṣāba llāhu bika khayran' (Allah wanted good for you)." In al-Asās: "'aṣāba llāhu taʿālā bika khayran': He wanted it for you; 'rakhāʾan ḥaythu aṣāba': gently, where he wanted."
(الْأَصْفادِ): the shackles. In al-Qāmūs: "ṣafadahu yaṣfiduhu, of the pattern ḍaraba yaḍribu: he bound him and fettered him, like aṣfadahu and ṣaffadahu. Al-ṣafad, with vowelled letters, is the gift and the bond; without the article it is a town in Syria; and in the pattern of kitāb it is what a captive is bound with, whether a leather strap or a fetter. And al-aṣfād are the fetters." So there is no sense in the words of some commentators in rejecting al-Jalāl, who explained al-aṣfād as fetters, when that commentator said: "It is known that the fetter is on the leg, so this explanation does not fit with His words 'He gathers their hands…' etc.; if he had explained al-aṣfād as shackles (aghlāl) it would be clearer." In al-Mukhtār: "ṣafadahu: he bound him and fettered him, of the pattern ḍaraba, and likewise ṣaffadahu taṣfīdan. Al-ṣafad, with two fatḥas, and al-ṣifād, with kasra, is what a captive is bound with, whether a leather strap, a fetter or a shackle. Al-aṣfād are the fetters, its singular being ṣafad."

* I'rab:
(وَوَهَبْنا لِداوُدَ سُلَيْمانَ نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ) The wāw is resumptive, and the discourse is resumptive, introduced to expand on the story of Sulaymān after having expanded on the story of Dāwūd. وهبنا is a past verb and agent; لداود: the two are attached to وهبنا; سليمان is a direct object; نعم is an inert past verb, for the composition of praise, and العبد is its agent; the one specified for praise is omitted because it was mentioned earlier, that is, "he". وإنه أواب: إن with its noun and khabar, and the clause gives the reason for the praise: the reason for his being praised is given as his being awwāb, one who returns to Him by repentance, or one who glorifies, returning to the glorification and bringing it back, for every muʾawwib is awwāb. (إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِناتُ الْجِيادُ) إذ may be an adverbial of أواب, or its governor may be نعم, or it may be accusative by an implied verb, that is, "remember, O Muḥammad, the time of the occurrence of this story". The clause عرض is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; عليه: the two are attached to عرض; بالعشي: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "occurring at that time"; الصافنات is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil), and الجياد is an adjective. It is preferable that the object be omitted, that is, "the horses", with الصافنات الجياد as two attributes of the horses. The apparent sense is that the display captivated him and it seemed to him that he could rely on these well-bred horses in his fighting the enemy to please his Lord, so it occupied him for a while from the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, to which he was devoted.
(فَقالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّى تَوارَتْ بِالْحِجابِ) The فاء is a conjunction; قال is a past verb with a latent agent; إن and its noun; the clause أحببت is its khabar. أحببت does not run on its original meaning but includes the meaning of a verb that takes عن, in the sense of "I preferred"; حب الخير is a direct object of that verb, or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); it is also said to be an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi). The wording of al-Samīn: there are several aspects to حب الخير. The first is that it is the object of أحببت because it has the meaning of "I preferred", and عن on this view means على. The second is that حب is a maṣdar with the augments dropped, and أحببت is what governs it in the accusative. The third is that it is a maṣdar of "you desire", that is, "a love like the love of good". The fourth is that it includes the meaning of "I turned", and so is transitive with عن. The fifth is that أحببت means "I clung to". The sixth is that أحببت is from aḥabba l-baʿīr, when the camel falls and kneels from exhaustion, and the meaning is "I sat away from the remembrance of my Lord", so حب الخير on this view is an object of purpose. عن ذكر ربي: the two are attached to أحببت, and the annexation is the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, that is, "from my remembering my Lord", or to its agent, that is, "from my Lord's remembering me". More on this verse will come in the section on rhetoric. حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; توارت is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she", that is, the sun; and it is said, the horses; بالحجاب: the two are attached to توارت.
(رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْناقِ) ردوها: an imperative verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, that is, "he said: bring them back"; علي: the two are attached to ردوها. فطفق is conjoined to an omitted clause, that is, "and they brought them back, and he began…"; طفق is a past verb of the verbs of commencement, which work like كان, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; مسحا is an absolute object of an omitted verb, that is, "he wipes a wiping", and the clause is the khabar of طفق; بالسوق: the two are attached to مسحا; الأعناق is conjoined to بالسوق. A very curious statement of Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī will come, in which he differs from the bulk of the commentators and which deserves consideration; see it in the section on benefits.
(وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمانَ وَأَلْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ثُمَّ أَنابَ) The wāw is resumptive; the lām prepares for the oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; فتنا is a verb and agent; سليمان is a direct object; ألقينا is conjoined to فتنا; على كرسيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ألقينا; جسدا is a direct object; ثم أناب is also conjoined, but after a delay. The discussion of the trial of Sulaymān and its examination will come. (قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي) رب is the one addressed, annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; هب is an imperative verb of supplication; لي: the two are attached to it; ملكا is a direct object; the clause لا ينبغي is an adjective of ملكا; لأحد: the two are attached to ينبغي; ومن بعدي is an adjective of أحد.
(إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ) The clause gives the reason for the supplication for forgiveness and gift. إن and its noun; أنت is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; الوهاب is the khabar of إن or the khabar of أنت, and the clause is the khabar of إنك. (فَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخاءً حَيْثُ أَصابَ) The فاء is conjoined to an omitted clause understood from the content of the discourse, that is, "so We answered his supplication and returned to him this stolen kingdom"; سخرنا is a verb and agent; له: the two are attached to سخرنا; الريح is a direct object; the clause تجري بأمره is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الريح; رخاء is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تجري; حيث is an adverbial attached to تجري or to سخرنا; the clause أصاب is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it.
(وَالشَّياطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; الشياطين is conjoined to الريح; كل بناء is a badal from الشياطين; وغواص is conjoined to بناء.
(وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفادِ) وآخرين is conjoined to كل بناء, brought in with it under the ruling of badal, being a badal of the whole for the whole; مقرنين is an adjective of آخرين, that is, "some of them were bound together with others in fetters". (هذا عَطاؤُنا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) The clause is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, that is, "and We said to him"; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and عطاؤنا its khabar; فامنن: the فاء is the eloquent fāʾ, and امنن is an imperative verb, that is, "give from it to whom you wish"; أو is a conjunction of choice; أمسك is an imperative verb conjoined to امنن; وبغير حساب: the two are attached to عطاؤنا, that is, "We gave you without reckoning or measure", in which there is an allusion to the abundance of the gift; or the two are attached to امنن or أمسك; it may also be attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl in the accusative from what preceded, that is, "while you are not called to account for it", because it is exalted above reckoning and enumeration. (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ) The i'rab of the like of this has been given many times.

* Benefits:
The discussion of these verses and of the trial of Sulaymān with the horses and the thoroughbreds is too large for the scope of this book and lies outside its range, but we shall try to allude to this trial, to what has been said about it, and to the lies and falsehoods woven around it which Judaism, leaning to desires, has concocted. Before we begin, we quote a passage from Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī that swept away all the falsehoods mixed up with this story, embroidered with the weaving of imagination. He said:
«The true interpretation, in agreement with the words of the Qur'an, is that we say: the tethering of horses was recommended in their religion as it is in ours. Then Sulaymān, peace be upon him, needed to go on a raid, so he sat and ordered the horses to be brought, and ordered them to be run, and mentioned: "I do not love them for the sake of this world and the share of the self, but I love them for the command of Allah the Exalted and for strengthening His religion", and this is what is meant by His words «عن ذكر ربي». Then he, peace be upon him, ordered them to be raced and run until they were hidden by the veil, that is, disappeared from his sight. Then he ordered the horses to be brought back to him, and that is His words «ردوها علي». When they returned, he began to wipe their legs and necks. The purpose of that wiping was several things. First, honouring them, for they are among the greatest helpers in repelling the enemy. Second, that he wanted to show that in managing policy and the kingdom he went so far as to handle matters himself. Third, that he was the most knowledgeable of people about the conditions of horses, their diseases and their defects, so he would wipe them, and wipe their legs and necks, until he knew whether there was in them anything that indicated illness. This interpretation we have mentioned fits the wording of the Qur'an and obliges us to none of those objectionable and forbidden things. It is astonishing how people accepted these silly aspects. If it is said: the majority interpreted the verse with those aspects, so what do you say of it? We say: we have two positions here. The first position is that we claim the wording of the verse does not indicate any of those aspects they mentioned, and it has become clear, praise be to Allah, that the matter is as we have said, so clear that no sensible person doubts it. The second position is to say: suppose the wording of the verse does not indicate it, still it is speech that people mentioned, and abundant proofs have been established for the immunity of the prophets from sin (ʿiṣma), and no proof has indicated the soundness of these tales.»
The legend of Sulaymān's ring:
As for what is reported of the trial of Sulaymān, the story of the ring, the devils and the worship of an idol in Sulaymān's house, the verifying scholars refused to accept it and said it is woven by the imagination of the Jews. The legends relate that the news reached Sulaymān of Ṣaydūn, a city on one of the islands, and that it had a king of great standing, fortified by the sea, whom no one could overcome. So he went out to it, carried by the wind, until he made camp there with his armies of jinn and men, killed its king, and took a daughter of his, among the most beautiful of people in face, and chose her for himself. She became a Muslim and he loved her, but her tears would not dry for grief over her father. So he ordered the devils and they fashioned for her an image of her father; she clothed it as he used to be clothed, and she went to it morning and evening with her maidservants, who prostrated to it as they were wont to do in his lifetime. Āṣif informed Sulaymān of that, so he broke the image and punished the woman. Then he went out alone to a wilderness, ashes were spread for him, and he sat on them repenting and humbling himself. He had a concubine, mother of his child, called Amīna, and when he entered for purification he would put his ring with her, and his kingdom was in his ring. One day he put it with her, and the rebellious devil who had shown Sulaymān the diamond when he ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis, whose name was Ṣakhr, came to her in the form of Sulaymān and said: "O Amīna, my ring!" and wore the ring, sat on Sulaymān's throne, and the birds, jinn and men gathered round him. When Sulaymān came asking for the ring, she denied him and drove him away, and he knew that the sin had overtaken him. He went about the houses begging, and when he said "I am Sulaymān" they threw dust on him and reviled him. Then he turned to the fishermen, carrying fish for them, and they gave him two fish every day. He remained thus for forty mornings, the number of days the idol had been worshipped in his house. Āṣif and the great ones of the Children of Israel disapproved of the devil's rule, and Āṣif asked Sulaymān's wives, who said: "He does not leave any of us while in her menstrual blood, and he does not wash after sexual impurity." Then the devil flew off and threw the ring into the sea; a fish swallowed it and the fish fell into Sulaymān's hand; he cut open its belly and there was the ring. He wore it and fell down in prostration, and his kingdom returned to him. He ordered the devils to bring Ṣakhr to him; they brought him, and he put him in the belly of a rock and closed it over him with another, then bound them with iron and lead, then ordered him to be thrown into the sea, and so on to the end of that legend, which resembles what the imagination of Shahrazād depicts in The Thousand and One Nights of tales of jinn and legends of bottles and the like. How fine are the words of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ in this regard: «What the chroniclers have reported of the devil's taking his likeness, gaining power over his kingdom and acting in his community with injustice in his rule, is not sound.»
What the scholars of Islam hold is that the cause of his trial is what is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Sulaymān said: "Tonight I shall go round to seventy women, each of whom will bring a horseman fighting in the way of Allah the Exalted." His companion said to him: "Say, if Allah wills." But he did not say "if Allah wills." He went round to them all, and none of them conceived except one woman, who gave birth to half a man. By Allah, in whose hand is my soul, had he said "if Allah wills" they would have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen.» Al-Zamakhsharī said: «This and the like of it is not objectionable.» What remains is His words:
«وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا»: what is it? What is its reality? Those who relate the legend as it stands, like al-Jalāl and other great scholars, say it is the jinni Ṣakhr; those who deny the legend are perplexed about the body that was cast on his throne. At times they say it is the half-man that the woman bore. They said:
«The half is the body that was cast on his throne when it was shown to him, and it was his punishment and affliction, because he did not make the exception (in shā' Allāh), through the eagerness that engrossed him and the wishing that overcame him. And it is said: he forgot to make the exception, as is sound in the ḥadīth, so that Allah's command and will concerning him might be carried out. And it is said that what is meant by the body cast on his throne is that a child was born to him, whereupon the devils gathered and said to one another: "If a child of his lives, we shall not be free of affliction, so our way is to kill his child or derange him." Sulaymān learned of that and ordered the cloud, which carried him, and he used to rear him in the cloud for fear of the devils. While he was busy with some of his affairs, the child was thrown dead upon his throne. Allah rebuked him for his fear of the devils, since he did not rely on Him in that, and he became aware of his error and sought forgiveness of his Lord. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا» etc…»
However, the matter is not one that can be decided or weighed by opinion; these are historical questions on which the statements conflict, and Allah knows best.
What is meant by "khayr":
The scholars and commentators also differed about what is meant by khayr in His words:
«إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي». Some said it is wealth, citing His words «إن ترك خيرا», that is, wealth, and His words «إنه لحب الخير لشديد». It is also said to be figurative, meaning the horses that occupied him and made him forget the remembrance of his Lord; or he called the horses khayr as if they were good itself, because good is attached to them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection.» And he also said of Zayd al-Khayl when he came to him as a delegate and became a Muslim: «No man was described to me and then I saw him but that he fell short of what had reached me, except Zayd al-Khayl», and he called him Zayd al-Khayr. In al-Qurṭubī: «He means by khayr the horses, and the Arabs call them so, and rāʾ and lām alternate, so you say inhamalat al-ʿayn and inhamarat, and khatalta and khatarta. Al-Farrāʾ said: khayr and khayl in the speech of the Arabs are one.»
Among the eloquent speech whose heaven poets gazed up at is His saying:
«هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب». Sulaymān used to bind the rebellious devils to one another in chains and fetters, for discipline and to restrain them from corruption. From al-Suddī: he used to gather their hands to their necks in collars. The ṣafad is the fetter, and the gift was named by it because it is a binding of the one benefitted; from it comes the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: «Whoever does you a kindness has taken you captive, and whoever treats you harshly has set you free.» And Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī said, in an ode in which he praises Abū Saʿīd al-Thaghrī:
همي معلقة عليك رقابها ... مغلولة إن العطاء إسار
(My aspirations have their necks hung upon you, shackled, for giving is captivity.)
And Abū l-Ṭayyib followed him, saying in an ode praising Sayf al-Dawla:
وقيدت نفسي في ذراك محبة ... ومن وجد الإحسان قيدا تقيدا
(I fettered myself in your shelter out of love, and whoever finds kindness to be a fetter becomes fettered.)

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ص وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ) «ص»: what was said about it has been discussed in detail, and more will come in the section on Benefits. The wāw is a particle of oath; «الْقُرْآنِ» is genitive through the oath wāw, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. The answer to the oath is omitted, most probably, its implied form being "Indeed it is inimitable (la-muʿjiz)" or "The truth has certainly come to you". More of the i'rab of this verse and what has been said about it will come. «ذِي الذِّكْرِ» is an adjective of «الْقُرْآنِ». The meaning of «الذِّكْرِ» is exposition, or honour, or admonition and reminder, and all of these are valid. (بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي عِزَّةٍ وَشِقاقٍ) «بَلْ» is a conjunction and a transitional break-off (iḍrāb intiqālī); «الَّذِينَ» is a mubtadaʾ, «كَفَرُوا» is its ṣila, and «فِي عِزَّةٍ» is its khabar; «شِقاقٍ» is conjoined to «عِزَّةٍ», meaning arrogance and tyranny, and «شِقاقٍ» meaning refusal to accept the truth. (كَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ فَنادَوْا وَلاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ) «كَمْ» is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object of «أَهْلَكْنا»; «أَهْلَكْنا» is a verb and an agent; «مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ» is attached to «أَهْلَكْنا»; «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» is the tamyīz of the predicative kam, and what is meant by «قَرْن» is a community. «فَنادَوْا»: the fāʾ is conjunctive, «نادَوْا» is a past verb and the wāw is the agent; the wāw is circumstantial; «لاتَ» is a particle resembling laysa, and the discussion of it and of the tāʾ attached to it will come in detail in the section on Benefits; its noun is omitted, its implied form being "the time" (al-ḥīn), and «حِينَ مَناصٍ» is its predicate, «مَناصٍ» meaning escape.
(وَعَجِبُوا أَنْ جاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ وَقالَ الْكافِرُونَ هذا ساحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ) The wāw is conjunctive; «عَجِبُوا» is a past verb and the wāw is the agent; «أَنْ» is a maṣdar particle, and with what follows it forms a maṣdar in the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "they wondered at the coming of a warner"; «مُنْذِرٌ» is a postponed agent, and «مِنْهُمْ» is an adjective of «مُنْذِرٌ»; the wāw is a conjunction; «قالَ الْكافِرُونَ» is a verb and an agent. In it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, to register disbelief against them, to intensify anger at them, and to signal that their disbelief drove them to this saying. «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «ساحِرٌ» a khabar, and «كَذَّابٌ» a second khabar or an adjective of «ساحِرٌ».
(أَجَعَلَ الْآلِهَةَ إِلهاً واحِداً إِنَّ هذا لَشَيْءٌ عُجابٌ) The hamza is for interrogation of wonder, that is, they wondered at this restriction, because in their ignorance and stumbling in evil heedlessness they measured the unseen against the seen. «جَعَلَ» is a past verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "he"; «الْآلِهَةَ» is the first direct object and «إِلهاً» the second; «واحِداً» is an adjective; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; «شَيْءٌ» is its predicate, and «عُجابٌ» is an adjective of «شَيْءٌ». Al-Jawharī said: «العجيب» is the matter at which one wonders, and so is «العجاب» with ḍamma, and «العجّاب» with shadda is more intense than it.

* Benefits:
1- The omitted answer to the oath and its implied form:
The discussion of the openings of the suras has preceded in detail, and we preferred that it is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "this is ṣād". As for the answer to the oath, they differed greatly about it, and the soundest of what we have seen is that it is omitted; al-Zamakhsharī and al-Bayḍāwī limited themselves to this. Al-Ḥawfī said its implied form is: "The truth has certainly come to you"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said its implied form is: "The matter is not as you claim"; and al-Zamakhsharī said its implied form is: "Indeed it is inimitable."
2- The discussion of «لات»:
«لات» is one of the particles that operate like laysa; they are «ما», «لا», «لات» and «إن», because of their resemblance to it in negation. As for «لات», its origin is the negative «لا», to which a tāʾ was added, either to feminise the word or for intensification of its meaning, and it was specialised for negating times. The addition of the tāʾ here is better than in «ثمت» and «ربت», because «لا» is carried over onto laysa, and laysa takes the tāʾ; hence the tāʾ was not attached to the «لا» that is carried over onto «إن». According to the majority it is two words: the negative «لا» and the feminine tāʾ, which was vowelled because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn al-Ṭarāwa said it is a word and part of a word, in that it is the negative «لا» and the tāʾ is added at the beginning of «الحين». It was also said that it is one word, a past verb. On this view, is it the past of «ليت» (from «يليت», to diminish), used for negation, or is it «ليس» with kasra on the yāʾ, the yāʾ having been turned into an alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa, and the sīn replaced by a tāʾ? Both views are reported in al-Mughnī. Its operation is agreed upon among the Arabs, and it has two conditions: that its two governed elements be nouns of time, and that one of them be omitted, the omitted one most often being the noun, as in «ولات حين مناص», that is, "the time is not a time of flight". Among the rare cases is the reading of some who read «الحين» in the nominative as its noun, with its khabar omitted, that is, "it is not a time of flight for them a time", and it was also read «ولات حين مناص» with «حين» in the genitive. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «لات» is used as a genitive particle for nouns of time only, just as «مذ» and «منذ» are.
Al-Mutanabbī followed this view in his words:
لقد تصبرت حتى لات مصطبر ... فالآن اقحم حتى لات مقتحم
(I have been patient until there was no more patience; now I plunge in until there is no more plunging.) Abū al-Baqāʾ said: Using it with the genitive is anomalous, yet the Arabs have used it with the genitive, and they recited:
طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان ... فأجبنا أن لات حين بقاء
(They sought peace with us when it was no time for it; so we answered that it is no time for staying.)

dervis-irab:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا وَاصْبِرُوا عَلى آلِهَتِكُمْ) The wāw is conjoined to an omitted clause whose implied form will come in the section on Benefits; it may also be resumptive, the discourse being resumptive, introduced to confirm their plotting after they dispersed from their assembly with Abū Ṭālib. «انْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ» is a verb and an agent; «مِنْهُمْ» is a ḥāl; «أَنْ» is a maṣdar particle, and with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the content of an omitted saying, that is, "they went off saying 'Go on and be patient'". Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that it be explicative (mufassira) of «انْطَلَقُوا», because it implies the sense of speaking. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because those who go off from an assembly of mutual speaking must speak and confer about what took place with them." In any case it is also in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and the meaning is "they went off saying to one another". It may also be a maṣdar particle which, with what follows it, is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "with 'Go on'". «اصْبِرُوا» is conjoined to «امْشُوا», and «عَلى آلِهَتِكُمْ» is attached to «اصْبِرُوا», with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "to the worship of them", meaning you have no power to overcome Muḥammad, so you have nothing but patience. What is meant by «الانطلاق» here is not walking but the loosening of their tongues with this speech, just as what is meant by walking is not ordinary walking but persistence in a thing.
(إِنَّ هذا لَشَيْءٌ يُرادُ) The clause gives the reason for the command to be patient; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; «شَيْءٌ» is its predicate, and the clause «يُرادُ» is an adjective of «شَيْءٌ». (ما سَمِعْنا بِهذا فِي الْمِلَّةِ الْآخِرَةِ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا اخْتِلاقٌ) «ما» is negative; «سَمِعْنا» is a verb and an agent; «بِهذا» is attached to «سَمِعْنا», and the reference is to the oneness of Allah to which Muḥammad calls. «فِي الْمِلَّةِ» is a ḥāl of «هذا», and «الْآخِرَةِ» is an adjective, what is meant by it being the religion of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. «إِنْ» is negative; «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction, and «اخْتِلاقٌ» is the khabar of «هذا», meaning fabrication and sheer lying. (أَأُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِنْ بَيْنِنا) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; «أُنْزِلَ» is a passive past verb; «عَلَيْهِ» is attached to «أُنْزِلَ»; «الذِّكْرُ» is the nāʾib fāʿil, and «مِنْ بَيْنِنا» is a ḥāl. They denied that Muḥammad ﷺ should be distinguished with this honour from among their nobles and chiefs. They repeated this idea often, saying: «لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم». They said that and repeated it many times to relieve the rage seething in their souls and the resentment tossing in their consciences.
(بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ ذِكْرِي بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذابِ) «بَلْ» is a transitional break-off from an implied statement, as though He said: "Their denial of the Reminder is not out of knowledge; rather they are in doubt about it." «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ, «فِي شَكٍّ» a khabar, and «مِنْ ذِكْرِي» an adjective of «شَكٍّ». «بَلْ» is again a transitional break-off, introduced to explain the cause of the doubt that has settled in their consciences, namely that they have not yet tasted the punishment; had they tasted it and experienced its affliction and endured its humiliation, they would have believed and would not have resorted to repelling certainty with doubt. «لَمَّا» is a particle of negation and jussive; «يَذُوقُوا» is an imperfect verb jussive by «لَمَّا», and the wāw is the agent; «عَذابِ» is a direct object, and its sign of accusative is an implied fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person, to preserve the verse endings. (أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ الْعَزِيزِ الْوَهَّابِ) «أَمْ» is a conjunction meaning «بل», so it is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) «أم»; «عِنْدَهُمْ» is an adverbial attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; «الْعَزِيزِ الْوَهَّابِ» are two adjectives of «رَبِّكَ».
(أَمْ لَهُمْ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما) «أَمْ» is a conjunction meaning «بل». The wording of al-Zamakhsharī and al-Bayḍāwī is similar. Al-Bayḍāwī said:
"As though, having rebuked them for disposing of His prophethood, in that they do not hold the treasuries of His mercy, which have no end, He followed that by saying that they have no part in the affair of this bodily world, which is a small portion of the treasuries of His mercy; so how could they dispose of them?" «لَهُمْ» is a fronted khabar; «مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; «ما» is conjoined to «السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ», and the adverbial is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of «ما». (فَلْيَرْتَقُوا فِي الْأَسْبابِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, it is the apodosis of an implied condition whose implied form is: "If they claim that, let them climb the ladders leading to the Throne until they are seated upon it." The lām is the lām of command; «يَرْتَقُوا» is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command, and «فِي الْأَسْبابِ» is attached to «يَرْتَقُوا».
(جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الْأَحْزابِ) The grammarians differed greatly in the i'rab of this verse, because it carries several possible analyses; we present the most important of them as follows:
«جُنْدٌ» is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are a host"; «ما» is an indefinite complete noun (nakira tāmma), an adjective of «جُنْدٌ» by way of belittlement, that is, "they are a paltry host", for «ما», when it is an adjective, is used for magnification or belittlement, and the latter is intended. You may also parse it as redundant. «هُنالِكَ» is a demonstrative noun in the position of the accusative as a locative adverbial, attached to an omitted element that is an adjective of «جُنْدٌ»; «مَهْزُومٌ» is a third adjective of «جُنْدٌ» or a second khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ. It is also permissible that «جُنْدٌ» be a mubtadaʾ, for which it is acceptable to begin because it is qualified, with «هُنالِكَ» its khabar; Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred this analysis, and we will give you his wording in the section on Benefits. «مِنَ الْأَحْزابِ» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مَهْزُومٌ».

* Benefits:
1- The difference between «لمّا» and «لم»:
We set down here the fine difference between «لمّا» and «لم», by which it becomes clear why «لمّا» was preferred in His words «بل لمّا يذوقوا عذاب». They share several things: being particles, being specific to the imperfect, negation, jussive mood, turning the verb to the past, and the permissibility of the interrogative hamza entering them. «لم» differs from «لمّا» in accompanying a conditional particle, as in «وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته», because a condition is followed by what is affirmed with «لم» and is not followed by what is affirmed with «لمّا». «لم» also differs from «لمّا» in that the negation of what it negates may be cut off, as in «هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا», because the meaning is that afterwards he did become something mentioned. «لمّا» differs from «لم» in that its jussive verb may be omitted, as in «قاربت المدينة ولما», that is, "and I had not yet entered it"; this is not permitted with «لم», and they took the words of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Harimī as poetic necessity, namely:
احفظ وديعتك التي استودعتها ... يوم الأعازب إن وصلت وان لم
(Guard the trust you were entrusted with on the day of the bachelors, if you arrive, and if not...) that is, "and if you do not arrive". «لمّا» differs from «لم» also in expecting the occurrence of what it negates, as in His words the Exalted «بل لما يذوقوا عذاب», that is, "until now they have not tasted it, but they will". Sībawayh distinguished between it and «لم» in this regard: «لم» negates an act whose occurrence is expected, and whose affirmative does not admit «قد»; «لما» negates what is expected to occur, whose affirmative has «قد» introduced to it. Among the fine differences is that you may not say «الحجر لم يتكلم» (the stone has not spoken), but you may say «الحجر لا يتكلم» (the stone does not speak), because what follows «لم» expresses expectation, and that is impossible.
2- The story of ʿUmar's conversion to Islam:
History relates that these verses were revealed after the conversion of ʿUmar. The story of ʿUmar's conversion is closely linked in its episodes, with enjoyment and novelty in it, but it has many versions and different chains; we confine ourselves to the version of ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid, which Ibn Isḥāq transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ. It states that ʿUmar said: "I was far from Islam, and I was a wine-drinker in the Jāhiliyya, pouring it and drinking it. We had a gathering where men of Quraysh met. I went out looking for those companions of mine and found none of them. I said, 'If only I went to so-and-so the wine-seller.' I went to him and did not find him. I said, 'If only I went to the Kaʿba and circled it seven times, or seventy.' So I came to the Mosque intending to circle the Kaʿba, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing in prayer. When he prayed he faced Syria, placing the Kaʿba between himself and Syria, and took his place between the two corners, the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner. When I saw him I said, 'By Allah, if I listened to Muḥammad tonight until I hear what he says...' And it occurred to me that if I drew near to listen I would startle him.
