So I came from the side of the Ḥijr, and when I heard the Qur'an my heart softened, I wept, and Islam entered me." When ʿUmar became Muslim, that was hard on Quraysh, and twenty-five of their notables gathered and came to Abū Ṭālib and said: "You are our elder and chief, and you know what these fools have done", meaning those who had entered Islam, "and we have come to you to judge between us and your nephew." He summoned him and said to him: "O son of my brother, these are your people; they ask you for fairness and justice, so do not lean wholly against your people." The Prophet said: "What are you asking of me?" They said: "Leave us and leave mention of our gods, and we shall leave you and your God." He said: "Do you see that if I give you what you ask, will you give me one word by which you will rule the Arabs and the non-Arabs will submit to you?" They said: "Yes, and ten like it." He said: "Say: There is no god but Allah." They stood up, and the notables among them went off. By this, the conjunction we alluded to in the i'rab of «وانطلق الملأ منهم» and so on was made clear. [Translator's note: the source prints «تبيز» for «تبين» here, apparently a typographical slip; translated as "was made clear".]
3- The text of Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording:
We promised you to quote the text of Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording in the i'rab of His words «جند ما هنالك مهزوم من الأحزاب». He said: "«جند» is a mubtadaʾ, «ما» is redundant, «هنالك» is an adjective and «مهزوم» is the khabar. It is also permissible that «هنالك» be an adverbial of «مهزوم», and «من الأحزاب» may be an adjective of «مجند», or be attached to «مهزوم», or be an adjective of «مهزوم»." [Translator's note: «لمجند» is printed in the source; translated as "of «جند»".]

dervis-irab:41-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِنُصْبٍ): al-nuṣb, with ḍamma then sukūn, with fatḥa then sukūn, and with two ḍammas, is affliction and trial. It is said to be the plural of naṣab like asad and usd, and it is said to be a dialectal variant of al-naṣab. Much has already been said on this root.
(ضِغْثاً): a bundle of fresh grass and twigs. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-ḍighth, with kasra, is a handful of grass mixing green with dry; iḍṭaghathahu: he gathered it as firewood; aḍghāth aḥlām are dreams whose interpretation is not sound because of their confusion (and they have been discussed before); and al-taḍghīth is what the rain has moistened of earth and plants." In the proverb: «ḍighth ʿalā ibbālih». Al-ibbāla, with shadda, is a bundle of grass and firewood, and its meaning is one calamity on top of another; it is also used as a proverb for the man whose companion bears an unpleasantness and then he adds more of it.

* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ) Conjoined to «اذكر عبدنا داود». This was not mentioned in the story of Sulaymān because of the perfect connection between Sulaymān and Dāwūd, as if their story were one story. اذكر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; عبدنا is the direct object of اذكر; أيوب is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of عبدنا; the adverbial إذ is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from أيوب, and the clause نادى is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it, its agent being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to أيوب «[Translator's note: the source says "referring to Dāwūd" (يعود على داود); the context shows Ayyūb is meant]»; ربه is a direct object.
(أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذابٍ) أن and what is within its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "by the fact that Satan has touched me", relating the words with which he called his Lord in their own wording; otherwise it would have been said "that he touched him". مسني الشيطان: a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; بنصب: the two are attached to مسني; عذاب is conjoined to نصب. The secret of ascribing the touch to Satan, despite the immunity of the prophets from Satan's touching them and gaining power over them, will come in the section on benefits, as will what is mentioned of the cause of his affliction.
(ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هذا مُغْتَسَلٌ بارِدٌ وَشَرابٌ) Speech quoted from an omitted saying, that is, "and it was said to him". اركض is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", and the meaning of اركض is "strike"; برجلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اركض, and the object of اركض is omitted, that is, "the earth". In the lexicons: "He rakaḍa the earth and the garment: he struck them with his foot", that is, it is transitive in this sense. هذا is a mubtadaʾ and مغتسل is a khabar; it is a noun of place for the water with which one washes, the water being named after its place figuratively, the relation being locality; بارد is an adjective of مغتسل; شراب is conjoined. (وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) Conjoined to what preceded, as the situation required, as if it were said: "So he washed and drank, and thereby We removed the harm that was on him and wiped away from him the pains that had befallen him." وهبنا is a verb and agent; له: the two are attached to وهبنا; أهله is a direct object; ومثلهم is conjoined to أهله; the adverbial is attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being with them"; رحمة is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi); منا is an adjective of رحمة; ذكرى is conjoined to رحمة, that is, the gift was for mercy to him and for a reminder to those of understanding; ولأولي is an adjective of ذكرى «[Translator's note: the source says "adjective" (نعت) here, though لأولي is a preposition and its genitive noun]»; الألباب is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً فَاضْرِبْ بِهِ وَلا تَحْنَثْ) وخذ is conjoined to what preceded; بيدك: the two are attached to خذ; ضغثا is a direct object; فاضرب is conjoined to خذ; به: the two are attached to اضرب, and the object is omitted, that is, "your wife"; ولا تحنث is conjoined to اضرب; لا is prohibitive and تحنت «[Translator's note: so spelt in the source, for تحنث]» is an imperfect verb jussive by لا. The discussion of his striking his wife will come in the section on benefits. (إِنَّا وَجَدْناهُ صابِراً نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ) إن and its noun; the clause وجدناه is a verb, agent and first direct object; صابرا is a second direct object; نعم العبد is a verb and agent, and the one specified for praise is omitted because it is known, that is, "he"; وإنه أواب: إن with its noun and khabar, and the clause gives the reason for praising him.

* Benefits:
What touched him of affliction and torment is ascribed to Satan, although it is a primary axiom that Satan is not given power over the prophets, as good manners towards Allah, because Satan used to whisper to him and entice him to aversion and impatience. It is mentioned, as the cause of Ayyūb's affliction, that a man sought his help against a wrongdoer and he did not help him; and it is said that his livestock were in the district of a disbelieving king and he flattered him; and it is said that he was pleased with the abundance of his wealth. As for the story of striking his wife, he had sworn during his illness that he would strike his wife a hundred times when he recovered, because of her tardiness towards him one day.
In al-Qurṭubī: "There are four statements on the cause of his oath:
The first: what Ibn ʿAbbās related, that Iblīs met her in the form of a physician and she invited him to treat Ayyūb. He said: 'I shall treat him on the condition that when he is healed he says "You cured me", and I want no reward other than that.' She said yes, and advised Ayyūb of it, so he swore he would strike her and said: 'Woe to you, that is Satan.'
The second: what Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab related, that she came to him with more than the bread she used to bring him, and he feared her dishonesty, so he swore he would strike her.
The third: what Yaḥyā ibn Sallām and others related, that Satan misled her into urging Ayyūb to slaughter a lamb as a means of drawing near to him, and that he would be healed. She mentioned that to him, so he swore to strike her a hundred times if he recovered.
The fourth: that she sold her braids for two loaves when she found nothing to carry to Ayyūb, and Ayyūb used to lean on her when he wanted to stand; for that reason he swore to strike her. When Allah healed him, He commanded him to take a bundle and strike her with it, so he took a hundred panicle stalks and struck her once with them."
The story of Ayyūb's patience falls within the aims of stories in the Qur'an, and the loftiest of those aims is establishing the particular, pure religious creed, whose enduring home is the conscience and the inner feeling. The call to hold fast to patience and to take refuge in it was not merely for its religious sanctity, but for the broadening of the horizons of the soul and the opening of the gates of knowledge before the self.

dervis-irab:45-48.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ) The wāw is a conjunction; اذكر is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you", that is, "remember, O Muḥammad, their patience over what befell them and their steadfastness in their beliefs, and take them as an example"; عبادنا is a direct object; إبراهيم is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān; إسحاق and يعقوب are conjoined to إبراهيم; أولي الأيد, that is, "possessors of hands", is a direct object (the meaning of أولي الأيد will be discussed at length in the section on rhetoric); الأبصار is conjoined to الأيد.
(إِنَّا أَخْلَصْناهُمْ بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ) The clause gives the reason for the highness of rank with which they were described and their elevation through knowledge and deed. إن and its noun, and the clause أخلصناهم is the khabar of إنا; بخالصة: the two are attached to أخلصناهم, and the باء is either causal, if أخلصناهم means "We made them pure", or for transitivity, if أخلصناهم means "We singled them out"; خالصة is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is, "by a pure quality"; and ذكرى الدار may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ or a badal from خالصة. If خالصة is taken as implying the sense of sincerity (ikhlāṣ), then ذكرى is a direct object of خالصة; if it is a maṣdar with the sense of purity (khulūṣ), then ذكرى is its agent. That makes four aspects for it. As for the annexation of ذكرى to الدار, it is an annexation of the maṣdar to its object, that is, "their remembrance of the Hereafter". There are multiple readings here, to be consulted in the longer works.
(وَإِنَّهُمْ عِنْدَنا لَمِنَ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ الْأَخْيارِ) وإنهم: إن with its noun; عندنا is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; the lām in لمن is the shifted lām; من المصطفين is the khabar of إنهم; الأخيار is an adjective. (وَاذْكُرْ إِسْماعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الْأَخْيارِ) واذكر is conjoined to what preceded; اذكر إسماعيل: a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; اليسع and ذا الكفل are conjoined to إسماعيل; كل is a mubtadaʾ, permissible to begin with because of the sense of generality it contains; من الأخيار is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
There is a kināya (allusion) in His words «أولي الأيد والأبصار», which is an allusion to righteous deed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Possessors of deeds and reflection, as if those who do not do the deeds of the Hereafter, do not strive in Allah's cause, do not reflect as the people of religions reflect, and have no insight, are in the position of the crippled who cannot use their limbs and of those robbed of their minds who have no insight." There is also in it the art of ta'rīḍ (indirect hint), that whoever is not among the workers for Allah and not among those with insight into Allah's religion deserves rebuke and the worst censure. Al-aydī is the plural of yad, which is the limb, so the allusion by it is because all deeds are performed with it; and if it is a plural of yad in the sense of favour, then it is a mursal trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, which has been discussed before, since the hand is the cause of favour. The yāʾ was dropped in the script of the muṣḥaf, content with the kasra in its place. Some explained al-ayd in the sense of strength; though it is permissible in terms of language, the context weakens its use in this sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its explanation as al-ayd from al-taʾyīd (support) is unsettled and not possible."

dervis-irab:49-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ): women who restrain their gaze to their husbands and look at no one else.
(أَتْرابٌ): of equal age. They were so named as if the dust (turāb) had touched them at one time. Al-Bayḍāwī says: "atrāb for their husbands, lidāt for them, that is, equal to their husbands in age, for love among peers is firmer." Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the equality be among themselves rather than with their husbands. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-tirb, with kasra, is the lida, the age, and the one born with you; she is my tirb, and tārabtuhā: she became her tirb." ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
أبرزوها مثل المهاة تهادى ... من خمس كواعب أتراب
(They brought her forth like a wild cow, walking gracefully, among five full-breasted girls of equal age.)
Someone has versified the meanings of this root, saying:
وضع تراب فوق صك ترب ... ضرب ترائب كذا والتّرب
مثلك سنا والتراب التّرب ... ترائب الشخص عظام الصدر
ومصدر لترب الشيء التّرب ... وجمع ترب الشخص في العمر التّرب وجمع تربة بضم التّرب ... أي قطعة من التراب فادر
(Putting dust over a document, tarraba; striking; the chest-bones, tarāʾib; likewise al-tirb, one equal to you in age; and al-turāb is al-tarb; the tarāʾib of a person are the bones of the chest; the verbal noun of tariba al-shayʾ is al-tarab; the plural of the tirb of a person in age is atrāb; and the plural of turba, with ḍamma, is al-turab, a piece of earth, so know it.) «[Translator's note: the verses are given as in the source, which is corrupt in places; the gloss follows the sense of the lexical items they list]»
(وَغَسَّاقٌ): what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. In al-Qāmūs: "ghasaqa l-jurḥ: yellow water flowed from the wound." And it is said: the ḥamīm burns by its heat, and the ghassāq burns by its cold.

* I'rab:
(هذا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to announce the end of the preceding stories and the beginning of another subject. هذا is a mubtadaʾ and ذكر is a khabar; وإن: the wāw is resumptive, and إن is a particle resembling the verb; للمتقين is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; حسن مآب is its postponed noun. (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوابُ) جنات عدن is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān of حسن مآب; مفتحة is a ḥāl from جنات عدن, and its governor is the verbal sense contained in المتقين; لهم: the two are attached to مفتحة; الأبواب is the deputy agent of مفتحة since it is a passive participle. Al-Zamakhsharī said, on the i'rab of this verse: "مفتحة is a ḥāl and its governor is the verbal sense in للمتقين; in مفتحة is the pronoun of the gardens, and الأبواب is a badal from the pronoun, its implied form being 'opened, they, the doors', like their saying 'Zayd was struck, the hand and the foot', and it is a badal of inclusion. It was read جنات عدن مفتحة in the nominative, with جنات عدن as a mubtadaʾ and مفتحة its khabar, or both as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, 'it is gardens of Eden, they being opened for them'."
(مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرابٍ) متكئين is a ḥāl from the هاء in لهم, and its governor is مفتحة; فيها: the two are attached to متكئين; the clause يدعون is either resumptive, to explain their state in it, or may be a ḥāl of what was mentioned; فيها is a ḥāl from the agent of يدعون, that is, "while they are in it"; بفاكهة: the two are attached to يدعون. Limiting it to fruit gives the intimation that their food there is not for nourishment and maintenance of the body but purely for pleasure and enjoyment; كثيرة is an adjective; شراب is conjoined to فاكهة. (وَعِنْدَهُمْ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ أَتْرابٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; the adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; قاصرات الطرف is a postponed mubtadaʾ; أتراب is an adjective of قاصرات. (هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الْحِسابِ) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and ما is a khabar; the clause توعدون is the ṣila; ليوم الحساب: the two are attached to توعدون; the lām is for reason, that is, "for the sake of the Day of Reckoning". I see that it is permissible to parse ما as a badal from the demonstrative, with ليوم الحساب as the khabar, and perhaps that is preferable.
(إِنَّ هذا لَرِزْقُنا ما لَهُ مِنْ نَفادٍ) إن and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; رزقنا is the khabar of إن; ما is negative, in the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī manner; له is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; نفاد is a noun genitive in form by من, in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of ما, or a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ) هذا is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the discourse is resumptive; its like was given shortly before. Ibn al-Athīr said: "This in this place belongs to faṣl (separation) which is better than waṣl (connection), and it is a firm tie between leaving one speech for another." The wāw is a conjunction and إن is a particle resembling the verb; للطاغين is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; شر مآب is the postponed noun of إن. (جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ) A badal from شر مآب or ʿaṭf bayān of it, and the clause يصلونها is a ḥāl; it is an imperfect verb «[Translator's note: the source says "and it is a direct object of an imperfect" (وهو مفعول مضارع), apparently meaning يصلونها is an imperfect verb]», the wāw is the agent and the هاء a direct object; you may also parse جهنم as an object of an omitted verb indicated by يصلونها. The فاء is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you want to know the reality of Hell, it is a wretched resting place"; بئس is an inert verb for the composition of blame; المهاد is its agent; the one specified is omitted, its implied form being "it". (هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ) هذا is a mubtadaʾ, and حميم and غساق are its two khabars; the clause فليذوقوه is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); the فاء is parenthetical; the lām is the lām of command; يذوقوه is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command, the wāw an agent and the هاء a direct object. The statements of the grammarians on this verse are much confused; the following is what Abū l-Baqāʾ said:
"هذا is a mubtadaʾ, and there are two aspects for the khabar. One is فليذوقوه, like your saying 'Zayd, strike him'; a group said this is weak because of the fāʾ, which is not in the sense of an apodosis like the one in «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا». As for حميم on this aspect, it may be a badal from هذا, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, 'it is ḥamīm', or a second khabar. The second aspect is that حميم is the khabar of هذا, and فليذوقوه is parenthetical between them. It is also said that هذا is in the position of the accusative, that is, 'let them taste this', then he began anew and said حميم, that is, 'it is ḥamīm'. As for غساق, it is read with shadda like kaffār and ṣabbār, and with light sīn as a noun for the maṣdar, that is, 'possessing ghasaq', or fiʿāl in the sense of fāʿil."
(وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْواجٌ) وآخر is conjoined to حميم and غساق; من شكله is an adjective of it; أزواج is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are", or an attribute of the three.
(هذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ) The clause is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, that is, "and it will be said to them when they enter the Fire". هذا is a mubtadaʾ and فوج a khabar; مقتحم is an adjective of فوج; معكم is an adverbial attached to an omitted second adjective of فوج, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in مقتحم, or from فوج because it is described; لا is negative; مرحبا is accusative as a maṣdar; بهم: the two are attached to مرحبا. In the negated clause there are two aspects: one, that it is resumptive, delivered as a supplication against them for narrowness of place; or a ḥāl, that is, "this is a throng rushing in, it being said to them: no welcome to them". In al-Qurṭubī: "The leaders said: «لا مرحبا بهم», that is, may their dwellings in the Fire not be spacious. Al-raḥb is spaciousness, and from it comes raḥbat al-majd and others; it has the sense of a supplication, and for that reason is accusative." Abū ʿUbayda said: The Arabs say «lā marḥaban bika», that is, may the earth not be wide for you nor spacious. The clause إنهم صالو النار gives the reason for their deserving the supplication against them; إن and its noun, and صالو النار is its khabar.
(قالُوا بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا فَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ) قالوا is a verb and agent, and the pronoun refers to the followers; بل is a particle of retraction; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; لا مرحبا is the quoted speech of an omitted saying, which is the khabar, that is, "it is said to you"; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause قدمتموه is its khabar; قدمتموه is a past verb, the tāʾ an agent, the mīm the mark of the masculine plural, the wāw for filling out the ḍamma of the mīm, and the هاء a direct object; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدمتموه. فبئس: the فاء is a conjunction; بئس is an inert past verb for the composition of blame; القرار is its agent; the one specified for blame is omitted, that is, "the Fire".

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَوْتادِ) : In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«الوتد» with kasra on the tāʾ is in the dialect of the Ḥijāz and is the most eloquent; its plural is «أوتاد». With fatḥa on the tāʾ is a dialect. The people of Najd make the tāʾ quiescent and assimilate it after the conversion, so «ود» remains. «وتدت الوتد أتده وتدا» (from the bāb of waʿada) means I fixed it in a wall or in the ground, and «أوتدته» with an alif is a dialectal form." In al-Asās: "He drove the peg, «الودّ» and «الأوتاد» with the mallet. It is said «تد وتدك» and «أوتده», and «انتصب كأنه وتد» (he stood up as if he were a peg), and «أذل من وتد» (more abased than a peg), and «وتد واتد» means firm. Among the figurative uses: «وتد الله الأرض بالجبال» and «أوتدها» and «وتّدها»; the mountains are the pegs of the earth. A bedouin was asked: 'What is the naṭshān?' He said: 'The thirsty man pegs.' It is also reported: 'something with which we peg our speech.'" In al-Qāmūs: "«الوتد» with fatḥa, also with vowelling of the second letter, and like «كتف»: what is driven into the earth or a wall, of wood; and in prosody, what is of three letters like «على»; and the small protrusion in the front of the ear. The plural is «أوتاد»; «وتد واتد» is emphasis. The «أوتاد الأرض» are its mountains; of lands, their chiefs; of the mouth, its teeth."
(الْأَيْكَةِ) : The thicket and the tangled, clustered trees; it has been discussed at length before.
(فَواقٍ) : With fatḥa on the fāʾ or ḍamma, meaning a return. It was read with both, and it was said that they are two forms with one meaning, namely the interval between two milkings of the milker and two sucklings of the suckling young; the meaning is that it has no pause even for the length of the «فواق» of a she-camel. In the Ḥadīth: "A visit to the sick is the length of the fawāq of a she-camel." In al-Mukhtār: "«الفواق» is the time between two milkings, because she is milked, then left for an hour for the young to suckle her so that her milk flows, then milked. It is said: «ما أقام عنده إلا فواقا» (he stayed with him only a fawāq). In the Ḥadīth: «العيادة قدر فواق ناقة». And His words the Exalted «من فواق» is read with fatḥa, that is, 'it has no respite, rest or recovery'." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī in al-Kashshāf: "«ما لها من فواق». It was also read with ḍamma: it has no pause for the length of a fawāq, which is the interval between two milkings of the milker and two sucklings of the suckling young. He means that when its time comes it will not be delayed by this amount of time, as in His words the Exalted «فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة». From Ibn ʿAbbās: it has no return or repetition, from «أفاق المريض» when he returns to health; and the «فواق» of a she-camel is the hour in which the milk returns to her udder. He means that it is a single blast only, not to be repeated or returned." This root has wonderful features, in that it is distributed over diverse kinds of meanings, and here we quote for you a summary of what appears of it in al-Lisān and al-Asās: "«ما بقي في كنانتي إلا سهم أفوق» — an arrow in one of whose notches there is a break or a slant; «فوّق السهم» means he placed the bowstring in its notch when shooting. You say: «لا زالت للخير موفقا، وسهمك في الكرم مفوّقا». «فوّقه»: he made a notch for it; «فاقه»: he broke its notch; «فاق قومه»: he surpassed them; «رجل فائق في العلم» and he «يتفوق على قومه»; «فوقته عليهم»: I made him excel; «أفاق فلان من المرض» and «استفاق»; and so-and-so is an addict who does not recover from drink; «تفوّق الفصيل أمه»: the young suckled its mother fawāq by fawāq, and the herdsman «فوّقه». Among the figurative uses: «تفوقت الماء»: I drank it little by little; «تفوّقت مالي»: I spent it slowly. He said:
تفوّقت مالي من طريف وتالد ... تفوّقي الصهباء من حلب الكرم
(I drained my wealth, new and inherited, as one drains the red wine from the vine's pressing.) «تفوقت وردي»: I took it little by little; «أتيته فيقة الضحى وميعته»: I came to him at the early forenoon; «خرجنا بعد أفاويق من الليل»: we went out after some portions of the night; «مجت السحابة أفاويقها»; «أرضعني أفاويق بره»; «فوّقني الأماني»; and «ما أقام عنده إلا فواق ناقة وفيقة ناقة». Perhaps in this there is sufficiency.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الْأَوْتادِ) A resumptive statement introduced to affirm the conditions of the tyrants and to explain the fates of the obstinate. «كَذَّبَتْ» is a past verb; «قَبْلَهُمْ» is an adverbial attached to «كَذَّبَتْ»; «قَوْمُ نُوحٍ» is the agent; «عادٌ» is conjoined to «قَوْمُ نُوحٍ», and «فِرْعَوْنُ» is likewise conjoined; «ذُو الْأَوْتادِ» means the possessor of firmly established sovereignty, and the metaphor of the pegs will be mentioned in the section on Rhetoric. (وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ أُولئِكَ الْأَحْزابُ) Likewise conjoined. As for «أُولئِكَ الْأَحْزابُ», you may make the demonstrative a badal of what precedes and «الْأَحْزابُ» a badal of it, or you may make it an independent clause composed of a mubtadaʾ, the demonstrative, and a khabar, «الْأَحْزابُ». (إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقابِ) «إِنْ» is negative and inoperative because the negation is broken by «إِلَّا»; «كُلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction, and the clause «كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ» is the khabar of «كُلٌّ». «فَحَقَّ»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «حَقَّ» is a past verb, and «عِقابِ» is its agent, in the nominative with an implied ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person, to preserve the verse endings.
(وَما يَنْظُرُ هؤُلاءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً ما لَها مِنْ فَواقٍ) The wāw is resumptive and the discourse is resumptive, introduced to affirm the punishment of the disbelievers of Mecca after explaining the punishment of those who preceded them in error. «ما» is negative; «يَنْظُرُ» is an imperfect verb, meaning "awaits"; «هؤُلاءِ» is a demonstrative indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as agent; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction; «صَيْحَةً» is a direct object and «واحِدَةً» its adjective; «ما» is the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī negative; «لَها» is a fronted khabar; «مِنْ» is a redundant preposition, and «فَواقٍ» is a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as the noun of «ما» or as a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ذو الأوتاد» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), meaning possessor of firmly established, secure sovereignty; its origin is in the steadiness of the tent drawn tight by its pegs. Al-Rufāda al-Awdī said:
البيت لا يبتني إلا على عمد ... ولا عماد إذا لم ترس أوتاد
(The tent is not built except on poles, and there are no poles unless pegs are set firm.) He says: a matter is not attained except through the availability of its means. He likened the dependence of the matter on its means, and the dependence of its means on something else, to the dependence of pitching a tent on the erection of the poles and the dependence of their erection on the setting of the pegs, tied with ropes. And after it:
فإن تجمع أسباب وأعمدة ... وساكن بلغوا الأمر الذي كادوا
(If ropes, poles and dwellers gather together, they attain the thing they strove for.) Then he said: if the ropes tied to the firm pegs are gathered, the poles are erected and the dweller is found, he reaches his aim; «ساكن» has the meaning of a plural, so the plural pronoun for it is correct. The meaning of «كادوا» is "they laboured": it is said «كاده كيدا» meaning he laboured over it, and the sense is "they attained the thing they strove to obtain". And al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said:
ماذا أؤمل بعد آل محرق ... تركوا منازلهم وبعد إياد
جرت الرياح على مقر ديارهم ... فكأنهم كانوا على ميعاد
ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة ... في ظل ملك ثابت الأوتاد
فإذا النعيم وكل ما يلهى به ... يوما يصير إلى بلى ونفاد
(What can I hope for after the House of Muḥarriq, who left their dwellings, and after Iyād? The winds blew over the sites of their homes, as though they had made an appointment. They had lived in them in the most luxurious life, in the shade of a sovereignty with firm pegs. Then all luxury and everything that diverts passes one day to decay and extinction.) He says: I wish for nothing of this world after them. Muḥarriq is Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī al-Lakhmī. «الإياد» originally is soil gathered around a basin, and the house protects it from rain and floods; it comes from «الأيد», meaning strength, or what supports a thing in general, also the shelter and the fortified mountain; «إياد الجيش» are its two wings, its right and left flanks; «الأيّد» is the strong. Iyād here is the name of the son of Nizār ibn Maʿadd ibn ʿAdnān, so he is the brother of Muḍar and Rabīʿa, and by it in the verse he meant the tribe; it is also reported «وآل إياد» conjoined to «آل محرق». «غني بالمكان», like «رضي», means he stayed in it. «البلى» is wearing away, and «النفاد» is extinction. He says: «تركوا منازلهم»: this is a resumptive clause to explain the negation of hope, or parenthetical between the two conjoined elements; and the clause «جرت الرياح» is resumptive, introduced to describe the state of the two tribes. He says: they perished, so the winds blew over the places of their homes; the winds' blowing over the sites of homes is because of the collapse of the walls that used to hold off the winds, and that is a metonymy (kināya) for their death. He indicated that their perishing was swift, as though it came at once, by his words «فكأنهم كانوا على ميعاد واحد». They had lived a stretch of time in the most luxurious life, and he likened the sovereignty through which came their might and assault to a tent pitched over them; the shade is the embellishing element (tarshīḥ) and the pegs the imaginative element (takhyīl). «إذا» is the sudden «إذا», that is, it suddenly appeared that all luxury is certain to pass away.
It was also said that there is no metaphor in the verse, and that Pharaoh would fix four pegs for everyone with whom he was angry, bind his hands and feet to them and torture him until he died. But the first is better and more eloquent.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِطَّنا) : Our share and portion of the punishment. It is originally from «قطّ الشيء», meaning he cut it, and from it comes «قط القلم» (cutting the pen). They said it in mockery, meaning "hasten for us a portion of what You promised us". «القط» is applied to a written sheet and a deed (ṣakk), because each is a piece, and a reward is called «قط» because it is a piece of a gift. Its plural is «قطوط», like «حمل» and «حمول», and «قططة», like «قرد» and «قردة» and «قرود», and in the small-number plural «أقططة», like «قدح» and «أقدحة» and «أقداح». In al-Qāmūs: "«القط»: cutting in general, or crosswise, or cutting something hard like the reed-case, like «الاقتطاط»; and short, curly hair, like «القطط» with vowelling; «قد قطط» like «فرح»; and «قطّ يقط» like «يمل», «قططا» with vowelling, and «قطاطة». «القطّاط» is the turner, the maker of reed-cases", until he says: "«والقط» with kasra is the share, the deed, the book of accounts, its plural «قطوط»; and the cat, its plural «قطاط» and «قططه»; and the hour of the night." Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: «القط» is the book with gifts. Al-Aʿshā said:
ولا الملك النعمان يوم لقيته ... بغبطته يعطي القطوط ويأفق
(Nor was it King al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him in his prosperity, giving the deeds of grant and excelling.)

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسابِ) A resumptive statement introduced to relate types of their evasion and mockery after His words the Exalted «فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه» (the verse) were revealed. «قالُوا» is a verb and an agent; «رَبَّنا» is a vocative muḍāf with the vocative particle omitted; «عَجِّلْ» is an imperative verb; «لَنا» is attached to it, and its agent is a necessarily latent pronoun whose implied form is "You"; «قِطَّنا» is a direct object; «قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسابِ» is an adverbial attached to «عَجِّلْ» also, or to an omitted ḥāl. (اصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ) «اصْبِرْ» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ» is attached to «اصْبِرْ»; the clause «يَقُولُونَ» is a ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "they say it". «اذْكُرْ» is conjoined to «اصْبِرْ», meaning "take comfort in the story of Dāwūd and restrain yourself from neglecting the matter of persevering against them and bearing their harm, lest he become a target of what he was targeted for"; «عَبْدَنا» is a direct object, «داوُدَ» a badal, and «ذَا الْأَيْدِ» an adjective of «داوُدَ», meaning possessor of strength; the explanation of «الأيد» has preceded. The clause «إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ» gives the reason for his being among the possessors of strength, that is, one who returns to the pleasure of Allah; inna with its noun and its predicate.
(إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْراقِ) Inna and its noun; the clause «سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبالَ», of verb, agent and object, is the khabar of «إِنَّا»; the clause «يُسَبِّحْنَ» is circumstantial from «الْجِبالَ». The secret of turning from «مسبحات» to «يسبحن» will come in the section on Rhetoric. «بِالْعَشِيِّ» is attached to «يُسَبِّحْنَ»; «الْإِشْراقِ» is conjoined to «بِالْعَشِيِّ», that is, morning and evening. The report of Ibn ʿAbbās about «العشي والإشراق» will also come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَالطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَهُ أَوَّابٌ) «الطَّيْرَ» is conjoined to «الْجِبالَ», or is a direct object of an omitted verb indicated by what precedes, that is, "and We subjugated the birds"; «مَحْشُورَةً» is a ḥāl, that is, gathered, glorifying Him. «كُلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ, for which it is acceptable to begin because of the sense of generality in it, that is, each of the mountains and the birds. «لَهُ» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أَوَّابٌ», and «أَوَّابٌ» is the khabar of «كُلٌّ», meaning one who returns often, an intensive of «آئب», that is, returning to Him with glorification. (وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ وَآتَيْناهُ الْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ الْخِطابِ) «شَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ» is a verb, an agent and a direct object, that is, "We strengthened it with troops and guards"; «آتَيْناهُ» is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; «الْحِكْمَةَ» is a second direct object, and «فَصْلَ الْخِطابِ» is conjoined to «الْحِكْمَةَ»; the meaning of «فصل الخطاب» will come in the section on Rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
These verses embrace several arts that dazzle the listeners, and here is the detail.
1- Shifting from the nominal form to the verbal:
In His words «يسبحن» there is a shift from the noun to the verb, and the point in it is to indicate renewal and occurrence, one thing after another and one state after another, as though the listener were present in that state hearing their glorification. Like it is the verse of al-Aʿshā:
لعمري لقد لاحت عيون كثيرة ... إلى ضوء باليفاع تحرق
(By my life, many eyes have been drawn to the light of a fire burning on the height.) Had he said «محرقة» it would not have had that effect.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq):
In His words «بالعشي والإشراق» there is a wonderful antithesis between the evening prayer and the forenoon prayer. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "I used to pass this verse «بالعشي والإشراق» and not know what it was, until Umm Hāniʾ told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her and asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer and said: 'O Umm Hāniʾ, this is the prayer of the ishrāq.'" From Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās as well, he said: "Do you find mention of the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā) in the Qur'an?" They said: "No." So he recited: «إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق». And from him also: "I did not know the forenoon prayer except by this verse."
3- The meaning of «فصل الخطاب»:
«الفصل» is distinguishing between two things, and speech that is clear was called «فصل», in the passive sense (bi-maʿnā al-mafʿūl). Its origin is that they say «كلام ملتبس» (confused speech), and «في كلامه لبس» (there is confusion in his speech), and the confused is the mixed, which is not clear because of its entanglement or its complexity; so its opposite was called «كلام فصل», that is, part of it separated from part. Its summary is that one does not err in the places of joining and separating; so in the word of testimony one does not stop on the thing excepted from, and one does not recite His words «ويل للمصلين» except joined to what follows it, nor «والله يعلم وأنتم» until one joins it to «لا تعلمون», and the like. The same applies to the places of conjunction and its omission, pronoun and overt noun, mention and omission, repetition and other arts, most of which have passed you in this book. It is also possible that «الفصل» be in the active sense (bi-maʿnā al-fāʿil), that is, the one that separates truth from falsehood, sound from corrupt, and the fat from the lean.
